html_value.text: Exploring geometric shapes across different cultures and their applications in everyday life.

Menu

  1. First Steps: Return to the main menu of the First Steps section.

  2. Volume 2 – Within Our Reach: In this volume, we delve deeper into the world of numbers, expanding our understanding through the lens of different cultures.

value.name: What do I need to build?
value.desc: From Machu Picchu to Asia and Africa, we look at what builders needed in order to measure and construct, with a practice exercise included.

value.name: When size matters
value.desc: In this text, we learn the rule that tells which of two numbers is greater or smaller, measure objects with a ruler, and see that two objects are fully equal only when they match in every characteristic we compare.

value.name: Greater or Smaller? (Game)
value.desc: A game to decide whether two numbers are in order, using greater (>), smaller (<) and much greater (≫) symbols, across four levels.

value.name: Comparing in more than one direction
value.desc: In this text, we learn to compare two objects in more than one direction, measuring width and height and comparing color, and we see that they are fully equal only when they match in every direction that matters.

value.name: Measuring in three dimensions
value.desc: In this text, we learn to measure solid objects in three directions — length, width and height — and we see that two cubes are fully equal only when all three measures match.

value.name: The History of a Theorem
value.desc: The story of the theorem — how professionals use it today without noticing, and who actually discovered it before Pythagoras.

value.name: Practicing with the Theorem
value.desc: In this text, we use the Babylonian Diagonal Triple (Pythagorean Theorem) to reinforce our knowledge through step-by-step calculations, charts and exercises — including spotting where a proposed equality fails.

value.name: Playing with the Theorem
value.desc: In this text, we explore the Babylonian diagonal triple (Pythagorean Theorem) through an application that facilitates its visualization.

value.name: The Theorem and the Circle
value.desc: We draw a circle with a string, place a right triangle inside it, and see how multiplication tables determine the angle — with charts and an interactive figure.

value.name: Trigonometry (Cosine)
value.desc: We define the cosine of an angle, watch it fall from 1 to 0 as the radius rises away from the horizontal, and practice with an interactive figure in the first quadrant.

value.name: Trigonometry (Sine)
value.desc: We define the sine of an angle, watch it grow from 0 to 1 as the radius rises away from the horizontal, and practice with an interactive figure in the first quadrant.

value.name: Where are we on a disk?
value.desc: We walk two legs of 200 meters each to build the pair (x, y), then use sine, cosine and the Pythagorean Theorem to locate any point on a circle.

value.name: Walking on the Circle
value.desc: Three charts plot the cosine and the sine across the first quadrant, and from them we derive that cos² (θ) + sin² (θ) = 1.

value.name: Playing with the Identity
value.desc: With an interactive tool, we move the angle through the first quadrant and watch sin² (θ) + cos² (θ) stay equal to 1 at every position.

value.name: Do we tangent the planet?
value.desc: We rearrange the cosine definition step by step until the tangent appears, and use the similar triangles in the circle to understand where it comes from.

value.name: Playing with the Tangent
value.desc: We divide the identity by cos² (θ) to discover 1 + tan² (θ) = sec² (θ), then practice with an interactive tool that moves the angle theta (θ).

value.name: Playing with the Cotangent
value.desc: We divide the identity by sin² (θ) to discover 1 + cot² (θ) = csc² (θ), then practice with an interactive tool that moves the angle theta (θ).

value.name: Our Position
value.desc: We build the graph of the tangent from the sine and cosine charts — using limits where division by zero appears — and practice with an interactive figure.

value.name: The other hypotenuse
value.desc: We define the secant of an angle, compare its graph with the tangent as the cosine approaches zero, and practice with an interactive figure.

value.name: The other opposite side
value.desc: We define the cosecant of an angle, compare its graph with the cotangent as the sine approaches zero, and practice with an interactive figure.

value.name: Functions and Trigonometric Relationships
value.desc: One application brings everything together — we choose a function or a relationship, move the angle theta (θ), and watch the triangle in the circle and the chart change together.
